profile.headline: Alaska's governor is courting data centers to create demand for North Slope gas, while most public comment and one senator push back.

sections.text: Gov. Mike Dunleavy has been recruiting data centers to raise energy demand and justify a gas pipeline. In January 2026 he was working with DigitalBridge, majority owner of Switch, and released an independent WilmerHale review of the state's $75 million commitment to a DigitalBridge fund. A bill requiring data centers to pay their own grid costs died in committee in May 2026.

Stak Energy has proposed a $500 million data center on about one square mile of state land near the Dalton Highway on the North Slope. It could eventually need 1 to 3 GW of self-generated power from North Slope gas, with construction planned from summer 2026 and operations by late 2028 (May 2026). The Pentagon has offered about 4,700 acres near Anchorage, Healy and Fairbanks for up to a dozen military data centers.

Public comments on the state's proposed 50-year lease for the North Slope project were mostly opposed; fewer than a dozen supported it (July 2026). The Fairbanks North Star Borough Assembly discussed a data center moratorium in 2026.

Sen. Lisa Murkowski (R) said she is "not a proponent of data centers" at JBER or Interior military installations because of Alaska's insecure energy base. Sen. Dan Sullivan (R) has pushed to bring data centers onto military bases in the state. In September 2026 both senators said they were open to AI guardrails.

The University of Alaska Anchorage College of Engineering opened a Master of Science in Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, and Engineering in fall 2025 (announced June 2025), aimed at building AI models for problems such as wildfire risk and energy resilience. UAA also hosts the NSF-funded Alaska AI Solutions Consortium, which held its first meeting in June 2025. In September 2026 the Board of Regents reviewed a draft AI policy requiring all three UA universities to write AI implementation plans; a final version is targeted for the November 2026 meeting.

profile.headline: Alabama's biggest AI story is Project Marvel, a $14 billion data center in Bessemer that was approved under a nondisclosure deal residents are still fighting.

sections.text: Gov. Kay Ivey created a Generative AI Task Force by executive order in February 2024; it delivered its final report in March 2025. In February 2026 she formed a Technology Quality Assurance Board to carry out its recommendations, including use of the NIST AI Risk Management Framework in state agencies.

The Bessemer City Council approved Project Marvel, a $14 billion, 18-building hyperscale campus, in November 2025. A revised plan in February 2026 expanded the site to 1,600 acres; the project is described as a 1-gigawatt data center.

A nondisclosure agreement released in July 2026 showed Bessemer officials had been required to destroy records about Project Marvel; it came out after environmental groups threatened to sue over public records. Birmingham has considered a 270-day moratorium on data-center activity. In September 2026 a conservative anti-data-center group brought a bus tour to Bessemer and McCalla.

In April 2026 the University of Alabama moved to create a School of Data Science focused on AI, the first such academic unit in the state. It is also opening the Alabama Center for the Advancement of Artificial Intelligence in its College of Engineering with a $2 million gift.

Sanders called the $6 billion AVAIO data center in Pulaski County "the largest investment in Arkansas history" (January 2026).

Google began a $4 billion data center on 1,100 acres outside West Memphis in October 2025, to be spent through 2027 and powered in part by a new 600 MW Entergy Arkansas solar project with 350 MW of storage. AVAIO plans a $6 billion data center in Pulaski County (January 2026), and a $6.6 billion project was proposed in the Arkansas River Valley (July 2026).

Pulaski County's Quorum Court approved a one-year data-center moratorium in May 2026 with an exemption, amid opposition to the AVAIO project. In September 2026 County Judge Barry Hyde vetoed new data-center rules the court had passed. Carroll County imposed a 12-month pause on June 16, 2026, and Union County a one-year moratorium from July 10, 2026. Little Rock passed its own data-center ordinance in June 2026.

In August 2026 the University of Arkansas, Fayetteville launched the Arkansas Materials Institute, with artificial intelligence among its five research areas. In April 2026 the University of Arkansas at Pine Bluff opened a university-wide Center for Artificial Intelligence and Data Analytics.

Tom Cotton filed the DATA Act, which would let data-center operators build and finance their own off-grid power plants so costs are not passed to residential customers. He said America "needs data centers to win the AI race against Communist China" but "we can't let data centers increase energy prices." In June 2026, as chair of the Senate Intelligence Committee, he asked the Justice Department to investigate what he called a Chinese Communist Party-led effort to shape U.S. opinion on data centers.

profile.headline: Arizona is one of the top two data center markets in the world, and in 2026 it paused the tax break that drew them there.

sections.text: Gov. Katie Hobbs signed HB 4168 on June 13, 2026. It stops the Arizona Commerce Authority from accepting data center sales-tax incentive applications from July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2029. Hobbs said Arizona is in the "Top Two market in the world for data centers". Her proposed data center water-use fee was left out of the budget. In September 2026 she declined calls to pause data center development itself.

Microsoft is expanding its five-building, $1.5 billion campus in Goodyear, and in May 2026 it paid more than $131 million for 100 more acres there. Project Blue, a $3.6 billion, 290-acre data center complex near Tucson, won Arizona Corporation Commission approval (4-1) for TEP to supply its power in December 2025. Amazon later withdrew from the project.

Tucson's City Council rejected Project Blue in August 2025 over water and power; Pima County approved the land sale and rezoning, and Attorney General Kris Mayes moved to block its utility deal. On December 11, 2025, Chandler's council voted 7-0 against a $2 billion AI data center after residents sent more than 250 emails.

Arizona State University was OpenAI's first university partner, in January 2024. In September 2025 the partnership was expanded to give ChatGPT Edu with GPT-5 to every ASU student, faculty member, researcher and staff member at no cost to them.

In September 2026 Sens. Mark Kelly and Ruben Gallego and Reps. Greg Stanton, Yassamin Ansari and Adelita Grijalva (all D) asked Interior Secretary Doug Burgum about 12 data center projects proposed on more than 17,600 acres of federal land in six Western states, four of them in Arizona. Kelly's "AI for America" plan (September 2025) proposes an AI Horizon Fund, paid into by AI companies, for worker training and power and water infrastructure.

profile.headline: California wrote the first US law aimed at catastrophic risk from frontier AI, and in 2026 it began restricting the data centers that AI runs on.

sections.text: Gov. Gavin Newsom signed SB 53, the Transparency in Frontier AI Act, on September 29, 2025; it requires developers of models trained above 10^26 FLOPs to publish safety frameworks and report critical safety incidents, from January 2026. Executive Order N-5-26 (March 2026) set AI procurement standards, a May 2026 order addressed AI job disruption, and a September 18, 2026 order convened experts to report within two months on strengthening AI safety law, including a possible "kill switch" for advanced models.

The largest data center proposed in California is a $10 billion, 330-megawatt campus of nearly 1 million square feet in Imperial County, put forward by developer Sebastian Rucci (reported April 2026). In September 2026 Newsom signed seven data center laws, including SB 886 and AB 2383, which require the Public Utilities Commission to set separate power rates so data centers cover their grid costs, and a water-use disclosure rule he had vetoed in 2025.

Imperial County supervisors froze data center projects for 45 days in 2026, then extended the freeze to a year. In Santa Clara, the Planning Commission delayed a GI Partners AI data center and required more public outreach. A 2026 PPIC survey found 51% of California voters oppose building new data centers and 73% oppose one in their own community.

Stanford's Center for AI Safety, in the School of Engineering, holds its 2026 annual meeting on October 5, 2026 under the theme "Trust, Verified". At UC Berkeley, the Center for Long-Term Cybersecurity runs an AI Security Initiative on AI risk-management standards, and the Berkeley AI Research lab held its 2026 graduate showcase in July 2026.

Rep. Jay Obernolte (R) co-wrote the Great American AI Act discussion draft with Rep. Lori Trahan (D-MA), released June 4, 2026; it would bar states from regulating AI model development for three years. The draft folds in Rep. Ted Lieu's (D) AI Grand Challenges Act, and Rep. Scott Peters (D) was involved in its release. In July 2026 Lieu introduced a bipartisan AI Kill Switch Act that would require labs to report security incidents and create a way to shut down their most powerful models.

profile.headline: Colorado passed the first broad state AI-discrimination law and then scaled it back, while its Front Range cities and counties pause data centers.

sections.text: Gov. Jared Polis delayed the 2024 Colorado AI Act to June 30, 2026 (signed August 2025). On May 14, 2026 he signed SB26-189, which repeals it and replaces its "high-risk AI" rules with a narrower law on automated decision-making in consequential decisions, effective January 1, 2027. In 2026 the legislature killed both a data center tax-break bill and a bill requiring data centers to pay for their own clean power.

Vantage Data Centers' Trident project in Aurora, 334 MW of IT capacity and about 500 MW total on 143 acres across from homes, would be Colorado's largest data center and can be approved without a public hearing (September 2026). QTS Denver-Aurora (177 MW) will be Xcel's largest industrial customer. Xcel's April 2026 large-load tariff for users of 50 MW or more requires 15-year contracts and an 80% minimum demand charge.

Larimer County (January 2026), Jefferson County and Boulder County (June 2026) adopted temporary data center moratoriums. Denver approved a one-year moratorium in May 2026, Longmont banned hyperscale centers over 100 MW in June, and Broomfield paused them for 18 months in July. Earthjustice and other groups intervened against Xcel's data center tariff in 2026.

CU Boulder leads the NSF National AI Institute for Student-AI Teaming (iSAT), whose funding NSF renewed for five more years in 2025. In July 2026 CU Boulder's research office awarded more than $200,000 to nine interdisciplinary AI pilot projects.

On September 25, 2026 Sen. Michael Bennet (D) proposed the AI Regulator Act, which would create an independent federal agency to regulate frontier AI models and social media, with power to pause the release of models that pose catastrophic risk.

profile.headline: Connecticut passed one of the broadest state AI laws in 2026 and has no AI data centers yet, while towns pass moratoriums anyway.

sections.text: Gov. Ned Lamont signed SB 5, the Connecticut Artificial Intelligence Responsibility and Transparency Act (Public Act 26-15), on May 29, 2026. It covers frontier models, AI companions used by minors, AI in hiring and watermarking of synthetic content, and was drafted with Attorney General William Tong and Sen. James Maroney.

Trumbull adopted a two-year moratorium on new data centers on September 9, 2026, as 365 Data Centers weighs converting a 15 MW site there for AI; Morris (two years), Groton and West Haven (one year) did the same. In February 2026 lawmakers heard SB 245 to repeal the 2021 data-center tax incentives Lamont signed.
Yale committed more than $150 million over five years (August 2024) to AI, including about 450 GPUs, faculty hires and seed grants.

Sen. Richard Blumenthal cosponsored the Hawley-Blumenthal AI Risk Evaluation Act (S. 2938, September 2025), requiring Energy Department testing of frontier models for loss-of-control and weaponization risk, and introduced the GRID Act requiring 20 MW+ data centers to supply their own power. In September 2026 Sen. Chris Murphy warned of "AI companies in a blind race to build a death machine first" and called for binding rules.

Connecticut's data-center incentive law, signed by Gov. Ned Lamont in March 2021, waives sales, use and property taxes for 20 to 30 years for projects investing $50 million to $400 million or more. By 2026 only Cigna had used it, saving about $17 million in sales tax on its Windsor data center. A proposed 1.5-million-square-foot hyperscale data center tied to the Millstone nuclear plant in Waterford was dropped. In his 2026 State of the State address Lamont said the state had told new data centers to "slow down" unless they add generation. In September 2026 Republican candidate Ryan Fazio called for repealing the tax break.

profile.headline: Washington, D.C. has a mayoral AI values order that governs how the city government itself uses AI.

sections.text: Mayor Muriel Bowser's Order 2024-028 (February 2024) set six AI values, an 18-month strategic plan and an internal AI Taskforce due to sunset on December 31, 2026. In July 2025 the city piloted deliberation.io, a public-consultation tool from MIT and Stanford, to gather residents' views on AI.

The District hosts no hyperscale AI campuses; the region's large data centers sit in Northern Virginia, mainly Loudoun County (July 2026). DC still shares the PJM grid, so capacity-auction costs driven partly by data-center demand reach Pepco bills. A study commissioned by DC's Office of the People's Counsel (April 2025) estimated the 2025/2026 auction would add about $10 a month, or 9%, to the average residential bill from June 2025.

Delegate Eleanor Holmes Norton said at a House Oversight hearing in June 2025 that "AI is a tool that can empower our public servants, but it is not a substitute for passionate and committed federal workers." profile.headline: Delaware's biggest data-center proposal, a 1.2 GW campus in Delaware City, was blocked by the state's coastal-protection law.

sections.text: Starwood Digital Ventures proposed Project Washington, a 6-million-square-foot, 1.2 GW data center in Delaware City with 516 backup diesel generators.

In February 2026 DNREC ruled Project Washington barred by the Coastal Zone Act, largely over its diesel generators. New Castle County Council adopted data-center rules in March 2026, and Starwood dropped its appeal in August 2026, so the project will not proceed as planned.

On September 18, 2026 Sen. Lisa Blunt Rochester and Sen. John Curtis asked Senate Commerce Committee leaders to hold a hearing with AI company executives on the capabilities and safety of their systems.

Gov. Matt Meyer signed HB 16 amending the state AI Commission law in May 2025, and in July 2025 signed a joint resolution to develop an AI Sandbox for corporate governance, biotech, healthcare, chemicals and finance, to give "space for visionaries and risk-takers to responsibly test cutting-edge artificial intelligence technologies in Delaware." His FY26 budget included $150,000 for AI career and technical education. In March 2026 the state launched a Responsible AI training course for state employees.

The University of Delaware opened the First State AI Institute in June 2025, led by Sunita Chandrasekaran, to build open-source research tools, with Unidel Foundation funding for AI hardware. In July 2026 NSF awarded UD $21.5 million over five years to lead the NSF AI Institute for Human-AI Cooperation, directed by Cathy Wu, with Delaware State, Penn, Florida and Princeton, focused on AI in physical therapy and rehabilitation.

profile.headline: Florida's governor wanted state AI rules the federal government would not write; his own House passed only the data-center half, and counties are pausing projects themselves.

sections.text: Gov. Ron DeSantis proposed an "Artificial Intelligence Bill of Rights" and a data-center bill in December 2025. The Senate passed the bill of rights (SB 482, including parental consent for minors on companion chatbots), but the House blocked it, saying AI rules belong at the federal level. The data-center bill, SB 484, was the only part to survive; DeSantis signed it on May 7, 2026. It requires AI data centers to pay for their own utility costs rather than shift them to customers. DeSantis has opposed federal preemption of state AI laws.

At least 16 Florida cities and counties had adopted or were considering data-center moratoriums by August 2026. Palm Beach County advanced a one-year moratorium and rejected Project Tango, a $2.6 billion data center planned for Loxahatchee. A 15-million-square-foot hyperscale proposal in St. Lucie County (Project Jarvis) was withdrawn in February 2026. Citrus and Lake counties moved to pause data centers, Hillsborough voted unanimously to draft a moratorium, and Orange County planned one in September 2026.

The University of Florida launched the fourth generation of its HiPerGator supercomputer in October 2025, a $33 million NVIDIA DGX B200 system with 504 Blackwell GPUs, which UF calls the fastest university-owned supercomputer in the country. UF built a campus-wide AI curriculum around the machine.

Rep. Byron Donalds, described as the Republican frontrunner for governor, said in 2026 that he disagrees with President Trump on federal preemption of state AI laws, and wants states able to regulate AI use of a person's name, image and likeness and to expand parental controls. Sen. Rick Scott has sponsored the ASK Act (first filed May 2023), which would require parental consent before minors use products with AI features.

In April 2026 the Fort Meade City Commission in Polk County unanimously approved a development agreement for a $2.6 billion, 4.4-million-square-foot hyperscale data center by Stonebridge on a 1,300-acre former phosphate mine, with about $140 million in county tax breaks over 10 years and power from Duke Energy. Water use was capped at a claimed 50,000 gallons a day, pending a separate water-district permit. In May 2026 Gov. Ron DeSantis signed SB 484, the Florida Hyperscale Data Center Act, which sets a permitting framework for data centers using 50 MW or more.

profile.headline: Georgia is one of the country's largest data-center markets, and power bills from that boom are now an issue in the governor's race, the utility-commission race and the Senate delegation.

sections.text: Gov. Brian Kemp backs data-center growth. In July 2026 he called a blanket moratorium "irresponsible" and "insane", said he is "more concerned about China winning this race", and added "We don't need to try to push these things where people don't want them." The state runs an Office of Artificial Intelligence. In March 2026 the state Senate passed a bill to repeal data-center sales-tax exemptions early; Kemp had vetoed a pause on those exemptions in May 2024.

OpenAI plans a $20 billion data center at an industrial site in Effingham County near Savannah (reported July 2026). Georgia Power's contract to serve it with 3.2 gigawatts reached its Public Service Commission review deadline in August 2026. The PSC has adopted a rule letting Georgia Power bill new customers above 100 MW, chiefly data centers, for the grid costs they cause.

DeKalb County extended its pause on new data centers through March 30, 2027, and Cobb County extended its moratorium into early 2027. Augusta-Richmond County extended its freeze on applications to mid-September 2026. A wave of bipartisan bills was filed in January 2026; by April, residents criticised the legislature for adjourning without acting on them. Data-center growth is a campaign issue in the 2026 governor's race.

Georgia Tech is building Nexus, a $20 million National Science Foundation-funded AI supercomputer announced in July 2025, planned for spring 2026 and rated at over 400 petaflops. Researchers nationwide can apply for time on it through the NSF.

Sen. Jon Ossoff wrote to FERC in April 2026 asking whether AI data centers are raising Georgia power bills and whether tech companies' promises to pay their own way are enforceable. On August 28, 2026, Sen. Raphael Warnock called for a moratorium on data-center construction in Georgia, lifted only for builders who guarantee no increases in residents' water and power bills, no pollution, no nondisclosure agreements and no "sweetheart tax giveaways to developers".

sections.text: In July 2026 Gov. Josh Green signed two AI laws. HB 2137 (Act 247) allows damages of up to $25,000 per item for unauthorized realistic AI imitations of a person. SB 3001 (Act 248) requires AI companion operators to tell users they are talking to AI and to encourage breaks during long conversations.

With more than $12 million from the NIH, the University of Hawaii Cancer Center and John A. Burns School of Medicine are converting a room at the Cancer Center into Hawaii's first AI data center, to analyze health data from Pacific populations (June 2026). A July 2026 UH study found rising heat and humidity threaten cheaper cooling methods for AI data centers.

Sen. Brian Schatz (D) introduced the bipartisan AI Labeling Act of 2026 with Sens. John Curtis and Mark Warner in July 2026. With Warner he also introduced the Artificial Intelligence Risk Management and Security Act of 2026, which would create a permanent AI Safety Board in the Commerce Department to set safety and security standards for the most advanced AI systems.

Hawaii has no large AI data center. A tracker lists 20 facilities totalling about 28.5 MW, the largest a 15 MW Smartronix site on Maui and the 6 MW AlohaNAP in Kapolei, which has a 1.5 MW expansion under construction. In June 2026 the University of Hawaii announced renovation of its Cancer Center data center for an NIH-funded Medical AI Core.

On Hawaii Island, Council member Heather Kimball's Bill 170 would separate industrial-scale data centers from ordinary data processing facilities in the zoning code, closing the route by which they could be built on industrial land. The council's Policy Committee advanced it 8-0 in July 2026; testifiers cited water and power use. In September 2026 action was deferred for planning commission review in October, with recommendations due November 4.

profile.headline: Idaho has one of Meta's AI data centers running, and a plan to build a far larger one on public land outside Boise is drawing opposition.

sections.text: Meta's Kuna data center, a $1.2 billion investment and the company's second AI-optimized facility, began serving traffic in September 2026. Rhea Data, a Nevada company, has applied to build a 4-million-square-foot, 600 MW data center and a roughly 450 MW gas plant on up to 3,700 acres of BLM land south of Boise; an environmental impact study is under way (September 2026).

In September 2026 Boise Mayor Lauren McLean called public-land sales for mega data centers "shortsighted" and asked for a state framework. The Idaho Sierra Club called the Blacks Creek plan "unacceptable".

The University of Idaho offers bachelor's and master's degrees in AI from fall 2026; Boise State launched an AI major in 2025. The Lemhi supercomputer, shared by Idaho National Laboratory and the state's research universities, supports AI and energy research, and Boise State is to take over its operation in late 2026.

Gov. Brad Little's January 2025 SPEED Act executive order set up a council to speed state permits for large projects, naming data centers among them. In 2026 he signed SB 1227, requiring a statewide framework for generative AI in K-12 schools from July 1, 2026. Earthjustice, the Alliance for Affordable Energy and the Union of Concerned Scientists are challenging it, saying Entergy and Meta are withholding projected energy demand and job figures. profile.headline: Rhode Island is focused on using AI inside state government, with a task force roadmap and a federally funded AI institute at Brown.

sections.text: Gov. Dan McKee's Executive Order 24-06 (February 2024) created an AI Task Force chaired by former Rep. Jim Langevin. Its January 2026 roadmap recommended AI workforce training, state-service pilots, a central AI guidance body and an AI-RI collaboration hub.
Brown University leads ARIA, a $20 million NSF AI research institute announced July 2025 and led by Ellie Pavlick, developing trustworthy AI assistants with mental-health care as the target use.
Sen. Sheldon Whitehouse, with Sens. Van Hollen and Heinrich, opened an inquiry on March 13, 2026 into eight companies including Meta, OpenAI and xAI over gas-powered data-center projects.

No large AI data center has been built or approved in Rhode Island. The main proposal is a business complex with a data center near the Fidelity campus in Smithfield. It is backed by Hanton City Investments LLC, a partnership that includes Revity Energy's Ryan Polumbo, and projects $59 million in revenue for the town over 30 years. The developer filed its application on May 4, 2026.

On May 5, 2026, the Smithfield Town Council voted 4-1 to bar data centers from every zoning district. Residents raised concerns about noise, water, electricity and conservation land. Because the Hanton City application was filed a day earlier, it may still be reviewed under the old rules. At the state level, six data-center bills were introduced in the 2026 session and none cleared committee.

profile.headline: South Carolina is landing billions in Google data centers while at least 13 of its counties have paused new ones, and the governor has declined to call for a statewide pause.

sections.text: South Carolina has no governor's executive order on AI; the Department of Administration published a state AI Strategy in March 2024 and runs an AI Center of Excellence for agencies. In September 2026 Gov. Henry McMaster said he would not call for a statewide data-center moratorium. No moratorium bill passed in 2026, but the budget requires large data centers to report water use. State-owned utility Santee Cooper charges higher rates to users needing 50 MW or more.

Google announced on October 13, 2025 a $9 billion investment through 2027 to expand its Berkeley County campus and build two campuses in Dorchester County, on top of $3.3 billion announced in September 2024.

At least 13 counties, including Colleton, Spartanburg and York, had passed data-center moratoriums by late September 2026. Colleton adopted a six-month pause on July 7, 2026 after about 500 people protested a proposed project; Spartanburg froze new applications in June 2026. Lexington, Kershaw and McCormick counties were considering pauses. Bills in 2026 proposed a statewide moratorium (S. 5526) and an end to incentives (H. 4583).
South Carolina State University, an HBCU, announced a collaboration with NVIDIA in June 2026 on AI education and workforce development.

In July 2026 Sen. Tim Scott, chair of the Senate Banking Committee, asked Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh to address data centers and AI at a coming hearing, raising their water and electricity use amid rising utility costs and resistance in South Carolina.

profile.headline: South Dakota passed a data-center "bill of rights" and refused tax breaks, and its two senators sit at the centre of federal AI policy.

sections.text: Gov. Larry Rhoden signed two data-center laws in 2026, in effect July 1: SB 135, the "Data Center Bill of Rights", makes data centers pay for the rate increases they cause, requires water providers to check large centres' use against supply, and bars the state from overriding local data-center ordinances. Lawmakers rejected a sales-tax exemption for data-center equipment in February 2026, and also rejected moratoriums.
In the 2026 Public Utilities Commission race, Democrat Frank Kloucek proposed a one-year ban on new AI data centers; Republican Don Haggar called it "reckless and pandering" (September 2026).
In July 2026 the Board of Regents asked for $20 million in one-time and $4.5 million in ongoing funding to build and maintain an AI system for the public universities, and adopted a new AI policy.

Sen. Mike Rounds co-chaired the bipartisan Senate AI Working Group behind the May 2024 AI roadmap and in May 2026 co-sponsored the CREATE AI Act. In September 2026 Majority Leader John Thune was drafting an AI-safety bill with Sen. Amy Klobuchar focused on catastrophic risks; its text had not been released.

Gemini Data Center SD LLC plans a data center of up to 500 MW on about 146 acres northeast of Sioux Falls, next to Xcel Energy's Split Rock substation; the city annexed the land in October 2025 and the council rezoned it 7-0 in January 2026, with closed-loop cooling required. Applied Digital's proposed 430 MW campus near Toronto in Deuel County, with up to $16 billion in investment, was declared unlikely to go forward in March 2026 after the Legislature rejected data-center sales-tax exemptions.

profile.headline: Memphis hosts xAI's Colossus supercomputers, and the fight over their gas turbines has made Tennessee a test of who pays for AI power and pollution.

sections.text: Gov. Bill Lee set aside $50 million in his February 2026 State of the State address to continue Tennessee's push on AI adoption. He signed HB 1847/SB 2128, effective May 7, 2026, which requires data centers with at least 50 MW of peak demand to pay the full cost of the electrical infrastructure serving them and bars utilities from raising other customers' rates for it. In July 2026 Lee signed on to the federal ratepayer protection pledge with TVA.

xAI runs Colossus in a former Electrolux factory in Memphis and Colossus 2 on Tulane Road, with a third site across the state line in Southaven, Mississippi. The Shelby County Health Department permitted 15 gas turbines producing 247.2 MW at the South Memphis site through January 1, 2027.

The Southern Environmental Law Center, for the NAACP and Young, Gifted & Green, appealed the county's xAI air permit over dozens of unpermitted turbines. In June 2026 the U.S. Justice Department asked a court to dismiss the NAACP's Clean Air Act suit against xAI, citing national security. Nearby residents filed a noise class action. On August 18, 2026 the Memphis City Council passed the first reading of a 12-month pause on new data centers; final vote October 6.

Vanderbilt University opened the Amplify Generative AI Innovation Center in its College of Connected Computing in February 2026, after making ChatGPT Edu available to all students and staff in January, and is launching an online Master of Science in AI.

Sen. Marsha Blackburn voted against the state AI-law moratorium in 2025. In March 2026 she released a draft national AI framework that would preempt state law, except state laws giving minors greater protection. In June and July 2026 she negotiated with the White House over narrow preemption in exchange for children's-safety bills such as KOSA and the NO FAKES Act, and pitched it to President Trump in the Oval Office.

profile.headline: Texas hosts the flagship Stargate campus and Google's largest state investment, and in August 2026 its governor froze new data center hookups pending a grid audit.

sections.text: Gov. Greg Abbott signed the Texas Responsible AI Governance Act on June 22, 2025, effective January 2026. It bans AI built for purposes such as behavioral manipulation or unlawful deepfakes and creates an AI Council and a regulatory sandbox. In August 2026 Abbott ordered an audit of every data center in ERCOT's interconnection queue, which holds about 474 GW of requests, roughly 90% of them data centers. ERCOT said the order "effectively pauses" new data center projects.

The Stargate campus in Abilene (Oracle, OpenAI, Crusoe) opened its first two buildings in September 2025 and is to reach about 1.2 GW with six more buildings in 2026, backed in part by a $2.3 billion JPMorgan loan. In 2026 Oracle and OpenAI dropped plans to expand the site further. In November 2025 Google committed $40 billion through 2027 for three data center campuses in Armstrong and Haskell counties, its largest investment in any state.

Hill County passed Texas's first county data center moratorium (one year) in May 2026, and Austin County adopted one in July. Caldwell County formally opposed water-intensive evaporative cooling in May 2026. In September 2026 the state Senate held a hearing on data center water use, and the attorney general demanded water-use reports from data centers in 18 counties.

UT Austin's Texas Advanced Computing Center is building Horizon with Dell and Nvidia. It is due to be the largest academic supercomputer in the US when Phase 1 enters production in fall 2026, with 300 petaflops and over 100 times the AI capacity of its predecessor, Frontera. UT says its 5,000 Nvidia GPUs give it the most AI computing power in academia; the Texas Legislature contributed $20 million.

Sen. Ted Cruz (R), chair of Senate Commerce, backed the 2025 10-year moratorium on state AI laws. In September 2025 he released a "light-touch" AI framework and the SANDBOX Act (S. 2750), which would let AI firms seek waivers from federal rules, and said preemption is not dead. In 2025, 16 Texas state senators led by Angela Paxton asked Cruz and Sen. John Cornyn (R) to oppose federal preemption of state AI laws.

profile.headline: Utah markets itself as a "pro-human AI" state, but a proposed 9-gigawatt data center set off a statewide backlash in 2026.

sections.text: Utah created the first state Office of Artificial Intelligence Policy in 2024; it runs regulatory sandboxes. In December 2025 Gov. Spencer Cox announced a $10 million "pro-human" AI initiative, and in February 2026 he named a Pro-Human AI Task Force. Executive Order 2026-03 (May 29, 2026) requires state agencies to review data centers against a framework covering water, the Great Salt Lake, air, ratepayers and public comment.

Box Elder County commissioners approved the Stratos Project, backed by Kevin O'Leary, on May 4, 2026: 40,000 acres in Hansel Valley needing up to 9 GW, likely more than $100 billion at full build. In June 2026, after backlash, O'Leary cut the site to just over 20,000 acres, and the first-phase permit was capped at 1 GW at Cox's request.

Hundreds of residents protested the Stratos approval in May 2026; the project sits beside the northern tip of the shrinking Great Salt Lake. In August 2026 Cox called for "major reform" of the Military Installation Development Authority, which had endorsed the project. Logan adopted a temporary prohibition on data centers on July 1, 2026, and Grand County a 180-day pause in July.

The University of Utah's One-U Responsible AI Initiative is a $100 million commitment announced by President Taylor Randall in October 2023. It is run by the Scientific Computing and Imaging Institute and funds cluster hires, fellowships, and seed grants, the first round totalling $386,855 across nine teams.

In September 2026 Sen. John Curtis (R) broke with the White House and called for congressional hearings with AI executives and a regulatory framework for AI companies. He co-sponsored a bill protecting AI-industry whistleblowers and the bipartisan AI Labeling Act of 2026. Sen. Mike Lee (R) argued in March 2026 for permitting reform to build the energy and infrastructure AI needs.

profile.headline: Virginia hosts the world's largest data-center cluster, and its new governor is moving to end automatic approvals as voter support drops.

sections.text: Gov. Abigail Spanberger signed a law in June 2026 shielding ratepayers from data-center grid costs. On September 18, 2026 she signed Executive Order 22, creating an AI Task Force, and proposed a framework for the 2027 session that ends by-right approval for data centers over 25 MW, bans nondisclosure agreements and raises water, noise and emissions standards.
Loudoun County has more than 130 operating data centers, with about 4 GW of installed IT capacity in 2025 and 2-3 GW more in development. They supply roughly 38-40% of county tax revenue.

The Court of Appeals voided the 2,100-acre Prince William Digital Gateway rezoning (up to 37 data centers next to Manassas National Battlefield) on March 31, 2026; QTS then withdrew its appeals. In July 2026 Prince William supervisors rejected the Dulles Cloud South proposal. Polling found Virginia voter support for new data centers fell from 69% to 35%.

Virginia Tech received a $20 million NSF grant in August 2026 for an AI-enabled cloud semiconductor lab, and its researchers joined three Department of Energy Genesis Mission AI projects in July 2026.

Sen. Mark Warner introduced six AI bills on July 21, 2026, including the Data Center Tax Accountability and Disclosure Act, tying bonus depreciation to energy and water disclosure. Rep. Eugene Vindman cosponsored a bill to repeal data-center tax breaks and voted for the Ratepayer Protection Act, which passed the House 417-3.

profile.headline: Vermont's Legislature passed strict data-center rules before any project arrived, and the governor vetoed them.

sections.text: The Legislature passed H.727, regulating data centers of 20 MW or more, 26-3 in the Senate. Gov. Phil Scott vetoed it on May 28, 2026, saying existing permitting already covers data centers; a House override failed 83-52, short of two-thirds.

Sen. Bernie Sanders introduced the AI Data Center Moratorium Act (S. 4214) in March 2026 to halt new AI data centers until Congress passes safety, labor and environmental safeguards. Sen. Peter Welch cosponsored the Power for the People Act (January 2026) on data-center grid costs.

Gov. Phil Scott signed Executive Order 04-26 in May 2026 creating a Vermont AI Economic Task Force chaired by Neale Lunderville, with 18 members named in August 2026. His office said "AI is the first technology in a generation that gives small Vermont employers the same tools the biggest companies use." In May 2026 he vetoed H.727, a bill regulating AI data centers, citing Act 250. In August 2026 he called on Congress to set national AI guardrails, saying "State governments alone can't do this."

No AI data center had been proposed in Vermont as of May 2026. Lawmakers still moved bills in 2026: H.727 on siting and ratepayer protection, vetoed in May 2026, and S.205, a moratorium on AI data centers needing over 100 MW until July 2030.

The University of Vermont received a $2.1 million NSF grant (July 2025) for IceCore, an AI supercomputer at the Vermont Advanced Computing Center for about 1,000 researchers, with research uses including analysis of large language model behavior. A second phase in 2026 adds NVIDIA H200 and RTX PRO 6000 GPUs. UVM also runs an AI Taskforce with seven working groups and a small-grant AI Innovation Fund.

profile.headline: Washington is studying data centers and AI more than it is regulating them: a big data center bill died in 2026, while three narrower AI laws passed.

sections.text: Gov. Bob Ferguson's Executive Order 25-05 (February 2025) created a Data Center Workgroup, which reported eight recommendations in December 2025. In March 2026 Ferguson signed three AI laws: HB 1170 (provenance or watermarking for AI-generated content), HB 2225 (companion chatbots, with protections for minors) and SSB 5886 (digital-likeness rights). A 19-member state AI task force released its final report in July 2026.

Quincy is the center of Washington's data center industry, with 53 facilities totalling about 1,073 MW; Microsoft runs 27 of them and Sabey 7. Data centers raised Quincy's assessed value to more than $6.1 billion in 2025 and pay 57% of its property tax. HB 2515, a comprehensive bill to regulate large data centers, passed the House 51-41 in 2026 but died in the Senate.

Seattle's City Council advanced a data center moratorium, with key votes scheduled for early June 2026 after grassroots campaigning. Opponents also organized a protest at an AI expo in Wenatchee in 2026.

The University of Washington launched AI@UW in February 2026, funded by a $10 million gift from Charles Simonyi in November 2025 and led by vice provost Noah Smith. The Allen School lists AI safety among its seven areas of AI work, and in September 2026 UW researchers including Franziska Roesner and Smith published a Q&A on AI risk.

Sen. Maria Cantwell (D), ranking member of Senate Commerce, led the July 2025 effort that removed a 10-year moratorium on state AI laws from the budget bill by a 99-1 vote. She later criticized the president's AI executive order for "overly broad preemption" that threatens states over protections against AI fraud, scams and deepfakes.

profile.headline: Wisconsin is home to Microsoft's Fairwater AI supercomputer and a $15 billion OpenAI-Oracle campus, and county after county is pausing new data centers.

sections.text: Gov. Tony Evers's AI work goes back to his 2023 Task Force on Workforce and Artificial Intelligence; in May 2026 the state launched WisTRAIN, about $7 million in federal grants for AI and manufacturing training. The Assembly passed a Republican data-center bill 53-44 in January 2026, but Evers signalled he would not back it.

Microsoft completed its first Fairwater data center in Mount Pleasant in June 2026, part of $4.7 billion planned there for 2024-2028, and called it "the world's most powerful supercomputer"; a second facility is due in 2028. Vantage Data Centers is building a $15 billion campus in Port Washington for Oracle and OpenAI. Wisconsin regulators approved power rates for Meta's Beaver Dam data center in May 2026.

By June 2026 Madison, Dane County, Manitowoc County and Superior had moratoriums; Winnebago County (June), St. Croix County (September) and Marathon County (September) followed, and Milwaukee's plan commission approved one on September 28, 2026. In August 2026 state regulators set back power lines for the Port Washington campus, and residents there keep contesting its noise, dust and costs.

In April 2026 UW-Madison named a founding dean for its new College of Computing and Artificial Intelligence, launched July 1, 2026 with $100 million in gifts and more than $50 million a year from the university. It is hiring 50 faculty, which brings AI-related hires since the RISE-AI initiative to more than 100.

In January 2026 Sen. Tammy Baldwin said data-center developers must commit that communities will not bear their energy and water costs; Sen. Ron Johnson called the grid impact a "very serious concern". Reps. Mark Pocan and Tom Tiffany said developers, not ratepayers, should pay; Rep. Glenn Grothman, whose district includes Port Washington, said "It varies in different situations."

profile.headline: West Virginia removed local control over data-center power sites to attract them, and landed a $45 billion Anthropic computing deal as counties organize against it.

sections.text: Gov. Patrick Morrisey signed HB 2014 on April 30, 2025, allowing off-grid microgrid districts for data centers and barring county and city ordinances over them. His August 2026 20-year data-center plan proposes an advisory council and setbacks, but a legislator noted "nothing has the force of law."

In August 2026 Morrisey announced that Anthropic agreed to spend about $45 billion over six years for 460 MW of computing at Nscale's microgrid campus in Mason County. Starwood Digital Ventures plans a $12 billion, 2.16 GW campus in the same county, and Penzance Management a $4 billion campus.

Residents formed Tucker United against a data center and power plant near Thomas and Davis, and Mason County United in Point Pleasant. In Mingo County, residents organized against TransGas mountaintop data centers (May 2026). Mason County's commission president said: "They can come into your county...And we can't do anything."
West Virginia University leads, with Pitt and Carnegie Mellon, an NSF industrial energy innovation hub funded at more than $320 million (July 2026), covering AI infrastructure among other work.

Sen. Jim Justice told the state Chamber of Commerce in September 2026 not to fear data centers but that companies must take care of water, power bills and noise. Sen. Shelley Moore Capito said she backs the Ratepayer Protection Act and wants early community engagement from data-center developers.

profile.headline: Wyoming wants AI data centers for its gas and power, and one campus near Cheyenne alone would draw nearly triple the state's current power demand.

sections.text: Gov. Mark Gordon signed Executive Order 2026-03, "Data Centers the Wyoming Way", in 2026. It sets eight priorities: water, wildlife, transparency, energy, grid protection, revenue, workforce and community investment. Gordon has argued for continuing to welcome data center investment rather than imposing a moratorium.

Crusoe and Tallgrass announced a 1.8 GW AI data center south of Cheyenne in July 2025, powered by Wyoming natural gas with carbon capture and designed to scale to 10 GW. By January 2026 Cheyenne had approved the project, Project Jade, at up to 2.7 GW of self-generated power, nearly triple the whole state's demand. Meta is building on a 945-acre site outside Cheyenne.

Residents petitioned for a 12- to 18-month moratorium on new data centers in Cheyenne to study water, air and infrastructure effects; the City Council rejected it 9-1 (2026). Cheyenne joined the national day of data center protests in July 2026, and Laramie residents organized against data centers in June 2026 although none are planned there.

A University of Wyoming AI commission began drafting campus guidelines on AI research and teaching in February 2026. UW's Advanced Research Computing Center launched two new high-performance clusters, SquareTop and GannettPeak, on August 25, 2026.

Sen. Cynthia Lummis (R) introduced the RISE Act in June 2025; it would clarify liability when professionals use AI and require developers to publish model cards. She called demand for AI "insatiable" and said she has worked to make sure companies powering AI data centers know they can come to Wyoming. She has also introduced a bill on grid connections for very large power users. Sen. John Barrasso (R) called Wyoming "America's energy breadbasket" for AI.
